relevance_note: The paper reports per-patient sex, age, medications and sleep-study results for 10 patients with SSADH deficiency: "Sleep recordings were obtained in 10 patients with confirmed SSADH deficiency."
method_note: Worked by reading the whole paper; a short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the rows and took table-row prefixes as spans, and I checked its output against Tables 1-4 by eye. Scope: all 10 enrolled patients have "confirmed SSADH deficiency" and get rows; no relatives are described. No ALDH5A1 variant (and no gene name) is printed and no variant is tied to any person (diagnosis was by "enzymatic assay, mutation analysis, or both" for the group), so the variants table is empty. Labels: the PID column of Table 1 holds bare numbers, so patients get 'Table 1 #<n>'; the text uses its own singular labels 'patient #3' (twice; once 'patient 3') and 'patient #10', so those two follow rule 1. Other patients appear in the text only in plural lists ('patients 2, 3, 7, and 10', 'patients 5 and 6', 'patients 7 and 10'), which I did not treat as singular labels. Patients 3, 7 and 10 were each studied twice (rows marked * = CNMC); age at last evaluation is the later study age, taken from Table 3 (header 'Age (years)'); treatment_summary lists the Table 1 medications per study. Contradictions: (1) patient 6 is 'F' in Table 1 but 'M' in Table 3 (the text says 7 male, 3 female, which matches Table 3); sex left 'not reported'. (2) The text gives 'age range 11-27 years' but Tables 1 and 3 list patients 1 and 2 at age 10. (3) The text says the repeat studies were 'separated by 3 years', but patient 10's ages are 23 and 27. (4) Table 4 orders the starred and unstarred rows of patients 3, 7 and 10 differently from Tables 1-3; I read PLMI per the row labels as printed (3* = 10.9, 8 = 14.1, 10 = 6.1), which matches 'Three patients had periodic leg movement indices greater than 5.0/h'. Table 2 is garbled in the conversion (its first data row is merged with the caption and the last with the footnote, and 'Bold: >2 SD' marking is lost), so I used no value from Table 2; REM-latency and REM% findings come only from sentences naming patients. Not recorded: group statements without names ('Five patients had decreased mean sleep latency', 'prolonged by 2 SD in 8 of 13 recordings', 'There was no evidence for significant sleep related respiratory disturbances', '5 of the 8 patients with decreased REM percentage were on no medications'); PLMI values below 5 and SOREM counts of 0 were not turned into 'excluded' rows; patients 5 and 6 'did not tolerate the daytime recordings' is not a phenotype. Medications (methylphenidate, levetiracetam, carbamazepine, antidepressants) were not used to infer ADHD, seizures or mood features. Checklist 'sleep disturbances' left 'not reported' for everyone: the paper reports polysomnographic findings (REM latency, REM%, MSLT latency, PLMI), not a clinical sleep complaint for any named patient; the 40% questionnaire figure refers to an earlier database, not these patients. No stacked ' / ' cells occur (the '5/5'-style cells in Table 3 are nap ratios for one patient).
